title: Descending the exchange property through a universal homeomorphism
statement:
Let $S'\to S$ be finite, surjective and radicial, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes with a constructible finite sheaf $F$ on $X$.
Suppose the direct image after base change to $S'$ is bounded
constructible and its formation commutes with every further base
change from a Noetherian scheme. Then the same assertions hold over $S$.
The notation refers to the canonical exchange morphism.

proof.text: Write $u:S'\to S$, $X'=X\times_SS'$, $Y'=Y\times_SS'$, $a:X'\to X$, $b:Y'\to Y$, and $j':X'\to Y'$. Work with the finite constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of the constructible sheaf $F$, with $F'=a^{-1}F$, and put $K=Rj_*F$, $K'=Rj'_*F'$. A finite morphism is integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft]. Radicial means universally injective; therefore the integral, radicial, surjective criterion [lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism] makes $u$ a universal homeomorphism. The projections $a,b$, and every further pullback of $u$, are universal homeomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change].

For any universal homeomorphism $v:V'\to V$ encountered here, [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] gives mutually inverse sheaf equivalences $v^{-1},v_*$. These equivalences lift to constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves: the action and its equations are carried by the inverse functors, and their units and counits are the underlying ones, as specified in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Thus both are exact and their units and counits are isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] to these two exact functors. Applying their sheaf units and counits termwise gives inverse derived equivalences $v^{-1}$ and $Rv_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], $\mathcal H^r(v^{-1}C)=v^{-1}\mathcal H^r(C)$; this equivalence reflects zero objects, cohomological bounds, and isomorphisms. In the square for $j$ and $b$, the canonical inverse-image square isomorphism and the derived adjunctions are the ones in [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with $L=j^{-1}$, $R=Rj_*$, $L'=j'^{-1}$, $R'=Rj'_*$, $G=b^{-1}$ and $G'=a^{-1}$. Both $G,G'$ are equivalences. Hence its mate is the canonical exchange isomorphism $\beta_u:b^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}K'$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism between the two objects.

Here is constructibility descent for an arbitrary sheaf $G$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y$. If $b^{-1}G$ is constructible, choose its finite stratification by reduced induced locally closed constructible subschemes, allowed by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. The homeomorphism $|b|$ takes this partition to a locally closed constructible partition of $Y$: opens, closed sets and quasi-compactness are preserved, hence so are retrocompact opens and their finite Boolean combinations by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Give each image stratum $Z$ its reduced induced structure; this choice is also allowed in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Put $P=Y'\times_YZ$. Its projection to $Z$ is a universal homeomorphism by step 1, and $P_{\mathrm{red}}\to P$ is one by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. Their composite is universal: after any base change its two factors are homeomorphisms, so their composite is a homeomorphism. The reduced inverse-image stratum chosen above is $P_{\mathrm{red}}$: locally, if $Z$ is defined by a radical ideal $I$ on an open affine $\operatorname{Spec}A$, both reduced structures are the quotient of the corresponding ring $B$ upstairs by $\sqrt{IB}$. Thus the two restrictions of $b^{-1}G$ agree on this stratum. Use [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence] to descend a trivializing etale covering of that stratum to $Z$; covering reflection is [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance]. On each descended etale object $V$, its pullback restriction is a constant finite module $M$. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant] the constant sheaf $M_V$ pulls back to that same constant sheaf. Full faithfulness of the module equivalence from step 2 therefore descends this isomorphism to $G|_V\cong M_V$. Thus $G|_Z$ is finite locally constant as a module sheaf, with the same finite module values. This proves constructibility of $G$ without a Noetherian assumption on $Y$.

By hypothesis $K'$ has cohomology zero outside some interval $[m,n]$ and constructible cohomology in that interval. Apply $\beta_u$ of step 2 and the cohomology comparison there: $b^{-1}\mathcal H^r(K)\cong\mathcal H^r(K')$. Reflection of zero objects gives the same interval $[m,n]$ for $K$. Apply step 3 to each $G=\mathcal H^r(K)$ to descend constructibility. This is exactly bounded constructibility by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes].

Fix an arbitrary morphism $t:T\to S$ with $T$ Noetherian. Put $T'=T\times_SS'$, $q:T'\to T$, $r:T'\to S'$. Then $tq=ur$. The projection $q$ is the base change of the finite morphism $u$, hence finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]; thus $q$ is affine and over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset T$ its preimage is $\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ a finite $C$-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. A finite family of module generators of $D$ generates it as a $C$-algebra, and $q$ is quasi-compact (affine), so $q$ is of finite type. Consequently $T'$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is a universal homeomorphism over $T$ by step 1, and the map $r:T'\to S'$ is therefore an allowed Noetherian test map for the hypothesis. No Noetherianity of $S$ or $S'$ has been assumed.

For a base morphism $h:B\to S$ write $\beta_h:h_Y^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rj_{B,*}h_X^{-1}F$ for the canonical exchange of [sbc-def-base-change-map], i.e. the unbounded module exchange $\Ex$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] of the cartesian square $(j,j_B,h_Y,h_X)$. Take $Y_T=Y\times_ST$, $X_T=X\times_ST$ and $Y_{T'}=Y_T\times_TT'$, $X_{T'}=X_T\times_TT'$, with projections $t_Y,t_X$, $q_Y,q_X$, and $j_T,j_{T'}$ the base changes of $j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the same schemes, with $r_Y:Y_{T'}\to Y'$ and $r_X:X_{T'}\to X'$ the induced maps, also form cartesian squares $(j',j_{T'},r_Y,r_X)$ over $(j,j',b,a)$, and $t_Yq_Y=br_Y$, $t_Xq_X=ar_X$ as morphisms to $Y$ and $X$. Thus the two pastings $(j_T,j_{T'},q_Y,q_X)\cdot(j,j_T,t_Y,t_X)$ and $(j',j_{T'},r_Y,r_X)\cdot(j,j',b,a)$ are the same outer square $(j,j_{T'},t_Yq_Y,t_Xq_X)$. Applying [lem-fin-module-exchange-composite-base-change] to both pastings and evaluating at $F$ gives
$$(Rj_{T'*}c^\Lambda_{t_X,q_X})\circ\beta_q^{(t)}\circ q_Y^{-1}(\beta_t)\circ(c^\Lambda_{t_Y,q_Y})^{-1}=\Ex_{\mathrm{outer},F}=(Rj_{T'*}c^\Lambda_{a,r_X})\circ\beta_r^{(u)}\circ r_Y^{-1}(\beta_u)\circ(c^\Lambda_{b,r_Y})^{-1},$$
where $\beta_q^{(t)}$ and $\beta_r^{(u)}$ are the exchanges of the squares $(j_T,j_{T'},q_Y,q_X)$ at $t_X^{-1}F$ and $(j',j_{T'},r_Y,r_X)$ at $a^{-1}F=F'$. Since the $c^\Lambda$ are isomorphisms, $\beta_q^{(t)}\circ q_Y^{-1}(\beta_t)$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\beta_r^{(u)}\circ r_Y^{-1}(\beta_u)$ is one.

The composite $\beta_r^{(u)}\circ r_Y^{-1}(\beta_u)$ of step 6 is an isomorphism: $\beta_u$ is one by step 2, and $\beta_r^{(u)}$ is one by the hypothesis, applicable because $T'$ is Noetherian by step 5. The first factor $\beta_q^{(t)}$ on the left is an isomorphism by exactly the mate argument of step 2 applied to $j_T$ and the universal homeomorphism $q_Y$ (and its pullback $q_X$), using [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences]. By step 6, $\beta_q^{(t)}\circ q_Y^{-1}(\beta_t)$ is an isomorphism; cancelling the isomorphism $\beta_q^{(t)}$ shows $q_Y^{-1}(\beta_t)$ is an isomorphism. Finally $q_Y^{-1}$ is conservative by the derived equivalence of step 2, so $\beta_t$ is an isomorphism. Since $t:T\to S$ was arbitrary with Noetherian $T$, this proves the required universal formation assertion over $S$, for the canonical exchange morphism, together with bounded constructibility from step 4.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S'\to S$ be finite, surjective and radicial, and let
$j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion of finite-type
$S$-schemes with a constructible finite sheaf $F$ on $X$.
Suppose the direct image after base change to $S'$ is bounded
constructible and its formation commutes with every further base
change from a Noetherian scheme. Then the same assertions hold over $S$.

proof.text:
By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], pullback
by a universal homeomorphism is an exact equivalence of etale
topoi. It preserves constructibility in both directions: the
underlying spaces are homeomorphic, and finite locally constant
sheaves correspond on every stratum under that equivalence.
The equivalence intertwines the direct-image functor for $j$
with the corresponding functor for its pullback, including their
derived functors. Therefore it detects boundedness and
constructibility of $Rj_*F$.
For any Noetherian $T$ and morphism $T\to S$, the pullback $T'=T\times_SS'\to T$
is again a universal homeomorphism by
[lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change].
Pull back the proposed exchange morphism to $Y_{T'}$.
Compatibility of exchange with composition in
[sbc-lem-base-change-composition] identifies it, through the
same equivalences, with the exchange over $S'$, which is an
isomorphism by hypothesis. The pullback equivalence is
conservative, so the original exchange is an isomorphism.
